title: Connected open containing two sections over a trait with reduced closed fibre
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with generic point $\eta$ and closed point $s$, and let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]). Let $\sigma,\tau:S\to X$ be sections, $f\circ\sigma=f\circ\tau=\mathrm{id}_S$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-section]. Assume the closed fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Put $F=f^{-1}(\{s\})$ and let $D$ be the connected component of $\sigma(s)$ in $F$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. If $\tau(s)\in D$, there exists an open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] containing $D$ such that $W\cap F=D$, $W$ is connected and nonempty, and both sections factor as scheme morphisms through $W$. The restriction $h:W\to S$ is flat, its closed fibre $W_s$ is reduced, and its generic fibre $W_\eta$ is connected and nonempty. In particular $\tau(\eta)$ belongs to the connected component of $\sigma(\eta)$ in $f^{-1}(\{\eta\})$.

proof.text: The DVR $R$ is Noetherian: every ideal is principal, hence finitely generated. The single affine chart $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ therefore makes $S$ locally Noetherian, and the affine-scheme quasi-compactness lemma makes $S$ quasi-compact. Thus $S$ is a Noetherian scheme, in the precise sense used by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem.

proof.text: Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FinitePresentation supplies the proved instance [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] → LocallyOfFiniteType f, by affineLocally_le and RingHom.FiniteType.of_finitePresentation. Thus f is locally of finite type without the cancellation theorem lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation. Apply LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian to f and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace to f to obtain IsNoetherian X, then its IsNoetherian.noetherianSpace instance gives the Noetherian underlying space directly. This uses the existing Mathlib matches of the finite-type-over-Noetherian and Noetherian-topology nodes; no separate minimal-closed-set argument is needed.

Every subspace of a Noetherian space is Noetherian (the subtype instance of Mathlib.Topology.NoetherianSpace). Indeed each descending relatively closed chain can be represented by intersections with descending ambient closed sets, using successive finite intersections, and hence stabilizes. Apply this to F and to the open subspace constructed below, including the empty-subspace case.

source.place: Tag 0052, lemma-Noetherian, first assertion and its elementary chain argument

proof.text: Let F be the closed point-set fibre and x its point given by σ(s), using the section equation. Let D be its connected component. By lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open the component of x in the subtype F is open, so its complement is closed in F. Since s is closed, F is closed in X; the image C of this complement under the closed embedding F → X is therefore closed. Put U = X minus C. The subtype image formula for connectedComponentIn gives D ⊆ U and U ∩ F = D. Let W be the connected component of σ(s) in U. The Noetherian component-openness theorem makes X locally connected by applying the same theorem to its open subspaces, so W is open in X. Connectedness of D and maximality of W give D ⊆ W, whence W ∩ F = D. The component W is connected and nonempty since it contains σ(s).

For either section φ the special point φ(s) belongs to W: use σ(s) ∈ D or the hypothesis τ(s) ∈ D and D ⊆ W. Every prime of the spectrum of a local ring specializes to its closed point. Continuity of φ and stability of an open under generization imply φ(z) ∈ W for every z. Thus the range of φ lies in the range of W.ι. The open-immersion lifting construction IsOpenImmersion.lift gives φW with φW ≫ W.ι = φ; its sheaf maps are the restrictions of those of φ. Apply this to both σ and τ.

Put h = W.ι ≫ f. Open immersions are flat and flat morphisms compose, so h is flat. The pullback map h.fiber s → f.fiber s induced by W.ι and identity maps on Spec κ(s) and Spec R is an open immersion, by base change of the open immersion W.ι. It follows that h.fiber s is reduced: isReduced_of_isOpenImmersion applies to this map and the assumed reducedness of f.fiber s. This comparison map is precisely the fibre-product restriction used in the source.

Let η be the zero prime of the domain R, the generic point. Apply lem-sbc-connected-generic-fibre-trait to h using connectedness and nonemptiness of W, flatness of h, and reducedness of its closed fibre. Its generic fibre is connected and nonempty. Put g = h.fiberι η ≫ W.ι and A = range g; continuity makes A preconnected. For either factored section φW, its section equation gives h(φW(η)) = η. The inverse of h.fiberHomeo η therefore gives a point of h.fiber η projecting to φW(η), and then to φ(η), so both σ(η) and τ(η) lie in A. The fibre homeomorphism also shows A ⊆ f⁻¹({η}). Maximality of the connected component in that fibre, via IsPreconnected.subset_connectedComponentIn, implies A is contained in the component of σ(η). This proves the last assertion.
